meta.face: Three clearly different men of Roman Africa with warm olive-to-bronze skin. VICTORIAN (centre): about fifty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a LONG, STRONG face and a LARGE, HIGH-BRIDGED, straight nose — deep NASOLABIAL folds from the nose to the corners of a firm, wide mouth, heavy-lidded, level dark eyes under thick straight black-grey brows, flat cheeks, a long, square chin; short grey hair combed forward in the late-Roman way; the gaze calm and unbending, toward us. THE ELDER BROTHER (left): about thirty, with a BROAD, ROUND face, full cheeks, a short, wide nose, round dark eyes, a short curly black beard; short tight black curls. THE YOUNGER BROTHER (right): about twenty, BEARDLESS, with a NARROW, TRIANGULAR face — a wide brow tapering to a small pointed chin, a fine straight nose, large, shining dark eyes; wavy black hair; looking up at his brother.
meta.basis: No likenesses survive; English Wikipedia has no article. The book, after Victor of Vita via Butler, gives the proconsul's answer to Huneric and the two brothers who promised to die together; its engraving shows Victorian standing before the enthroned king. The card leaves out the king and the torments. The clean-shaven, long-nosed proconsul and the two brothers' faces are our choices.
